Extreme Weather

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Going on the ground in the EC to see the devastation from floods - meeting up with gift of the givers, and other rescue teams and then branching out to the tell the climate change narrative.

Unique Selling Point:
Corene Conradie 079 226 6916 Dr Sooliman 071 365 2470.
We have permission to go out with the gift of the givers and see their relief efforts, they've asked us to go as soon as possible. So earlier rather than later...we'll go on the ground with them, and see whats happening etc meet people there in both towns Mdantsane and Duncan Village...

We need to hide the fact that we are looking at global warming and climate change - so we will add in the visuals from social media and put south africa in context with canada, colorado and siberia's strange weather - also look at where south africa lies on a global scale because of position so south of equator and why its been so extreme here.

Summary:
So it's January, and the rainy season only closes in April with March being the wettest month normally. So this is just the beginning of the coming wet season... eek. But various weather experts say our weather is becoming more extreme with this weeks forecasts saying there is a mixture of veldfire conditions in some parts, with powerful thunderstorms in others. "The South African Weather Service has issued several warnings of heavy weather across the Northern and Western Cape on Sunday. A mixture of veld fire conditions and potential thundershowers have been forecast. A level 2 warning for thundershowers has been forecast from Pofadder to Calvinia, and right down to the Cape Agulhas. Senior forecaster Luthando Masimini said this was due to two big low-pressure systems moving over those regions, which may cause flooding in vulnerable areas. Right next to them was a level 10 warning for potential veld fires in Oudtshroon and Ladysmith.
PLEASE SEE THE MAP BELOW:
https://www.weathersa.co.za/Documents/Corporate/MEDREL_20Dec2021_20122021115038.pdf
Map showing the amount of rain above normal... dark blue.
ALSO: JUXTAPOSITION Fish Hoek beach and EC Floods: the beaches were PACKED with beach goers this weekend, meanwhile in MTHATHA - people were drowning from floods. We can talk about la nina and global warming and this would be the nutgraph of the story with experts from weatherSA. There are a few people there, the one guy even does the weather in xhosa on facebook regularly.

Further information:
Then we come to the Eastern Cape which was hit hard this weekend: We can go there or we can send a camera man... its going to be hard to navigate with all the floods but a presenter could go and meet the camera man and get links, while i get the experts up here in joburg or i can go there too. Either way easy to do.

On the ground we would go speak to rescuers, and victims of the floods...


"The death toll from Saturday’s flash floods in the Eastern Cape has risen to seven. Mdantsane and Duncan Village were the hardest hit. Premier Oscar Mabuyane is working with ground teams to assess the full damage. His spokesperson Khuselwa Rantjie said the youngest drowning victim was just 19. Meanwhile, it's been confirmed that police rescue diver Captain Pierre Marx is the seventh death. Rantjie said the premier had conveyed his deepest respects to the late officer for his efforts."

Strangely enough I have friends who know Capt Marx and can try get his family to do an interview. He seems a hell of a guy - and the story of how he first saved someone before drowning himself is heroic to say the least.

I can contact my friend and the police contact Brigadier Tembinkosi Kinana 082 301 7699 about marx. He was part of the k9 search and rescue unit, and died in the line of duty. However, there are some excellent previous articles about him. his wife; https://www.facebook.com/michalene.b.marx

One thought is that we can go with the daily dispatch out there and see them in action too.

"Videos of heavy flooding in the Mdantsane area in the Buffalo City Municipality left South Africans stunned on Saturday night. Multiple bridges and roads were seen being completely engulfed by rapid water. Several houses and informal structures were also almost completely washed away. According to the East London Police, 53-year-old Captain Pierre Marx was attending to a complaint of drowning along with other rescue divers. Four people were swept off the Horse Shoe Valley causeway. Marx managed to rescue one, while his colleagues brought back three bodies “According to the report, the officers managed to take the three bodies across the stream. After a successful rescue of the complainant who is believed to be a local farmer, Captain Marx struggled with a strong current sweeping him despite attempts by his colleagues to rescue him. He disappeared in the heavy stream and only to be recovered in the early morning of Sunday the 09th January 2022.”

Script:


When the rains came there was a deluge: Mdantsane and Duncan Village, around East London, were underwater in less than 2 hours.
Corene: People are heartbroken people are still in shock.
As the rain continued falling, the unfolding disaster was captured on social media.
THAT SCARF OVER THERE IS WHAT REMAINS FROM ONE OF THE VICTIMS THAT DROWNED IN THIS WATER, FAMILY MEMBERS WERE COMING FROM THAT SIDE WHERE THERE IS ABOUT 144 FARMS AND THEY WERE GOING TO THAT SETTLEMENT JUST OVER THERE, IT SEEMS SLIGHTLY CALMER NOW, BUT THIS ENTIRE RIVER WAS OVERFLOWING WITH WATER, THEY THOUGHT THEY COULD MAKE IT BUT THEY DIDN’T.
In Mdantsane, 18 year old Yonela Pamla, her mother and 16 year old sister were inside their home - built on the floodplain. Corene Conradie is from NGO, Gift of the Givers.
Corene: They had no chance. 18 year old was swept with a very strong current inland Sunny, while her mother and the 16 year old had to climb a tree to to just to get away. And unfortunately, they couldn't save her and their house is right next to the river.
Yonela was just days away from receiving her matric results.
Corene: The mother of the deceased 18 year old was discharged from hospital and she came home to a site where Chef not only lost a daughter, but also where they home the place where they used to call home used to be. And she was in tears saying how will I bury my daughter right now? I don't even have money to buy a loaf of bread.
Last week’s flooding claimed 27 lives in the Eastern Cape, 8 of them in the Buffalo City Municipality. Among the dead, selfless K9 Search and Rescue diver, Pierre Marx. His death was vividly described by local councillor, Africa Maxongo.
Africa: So when the police were called in, to come to assist with drowning, that's when the captain Marx came he said to have saved, retrieved three bodies before he himself was entangled by a rope and himself drowned. So it said that we've lost five people.
Two of the dead were parents to 6 children; we accompanied Gift of the Givers to their home.
THE DISASTROUS WEATHER HAS LEFT NOTHING BUT DEATH AND DESTRUCTION IN ITS WAKE, MANY FAMILIES NOW FIND THEMSELVES IN A POSITION WHERE THEY’RE LEFT WITH NOTHING , THIS MIGHT NOW SEEM LIKE MUCH TO MANY OF US BUT IT IS A HOME THAT NOW DOESN’T HAVE A MOTHER AND A FATHER.
Nearby, we spoke to daycare owner, Nompumelelo Marhu.
Mac: So just tell me mama how has this affected you, you know with the floods as you run a daycare centre with kids?
Mama: This has affected me a lot, all my kids belongings were wiped out by the rain
Mac: All of it is gone mama?
Mama: all gone, stationary, even the uniform
Mac: have you gotten any help?
Mama: No, no.. no help at all
Mac: How far was the water, how bad was this?
Mama: It was up to the windows.
YOU MAY THINK THAT PERHAPS THIS IS ALL POLLUTION BUT IT ISN’T AND THERE WAS WATER THAT RAN THROUGH HER AND TOTALLY DEVASTATED THE COMMUNITIES THAT WE WERE ALONG THIS FLOOD LINE OR FLOOD PLANE AS YOU CAN SEE THERE ARE BEDS AND PEOPLES BELONGINGS THAT HAVE NOW BEEN TOTALLY WASHED AWAY AND THEY'RE NOT LEFT WITH NOTHING AND FAMILIES ARE DESTITUTE.
Worryingly, there was little to no warning of the coming disaster. Buffalo City spokesperson, Sam Ngwenya, says the law dictates that the alerts go to the provincial government first.
Sam: We were not part of the early warning systems from the South African weather services. But I think between 10 o'clock and one o'clock, we had a flash floods, heavy rains came down the city. They were areas that we quickly identified. And this was not one of them.
Mac you say that you will not have any warning systems why?
Sam: I think our disaster management team only alerted us an hour just before the actual storm that there is an early warning system. And by that time, it was too late. It became the biggest storm that we've had in this city for decades.
South African Weather Service forecaster, Mbavhi Maliage, says it’s up to the Province to warn its municipalities.
Mbavhi: She explains how the weather system works and its up to municipality’s to send out messages to villages. Disaster management was meant to be in communications with the villages.
The province's disaster and relief management team falls under the department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs or COGTA, but its website is incomplete, and if you call the emergency line you’re greeted with this: (this number no longer exists). COGTA Eastern Cape didn’t respond directly to our questions but sent this statement, “...natural incidents that result in disaster have been occurring much more frequently …which calls for pro-active and coordinated efforts to improve early warning systems and enable a swift response.
Sam: We are in a drought situation as a city, we’re implementing water restrictions. So I think it's part of the entire climate change system, because this incident has shown us that a lot is taking place within our vicinity.
Thats makes the need for early warning systems even more critical as we face what appears to be even more extreme weather occurring more frequently … what unfolded in the eastern cape last week – and in KZN in the past few days - comes at a time of extreme events in other parts of the world - like record breaking heat in Siberia, out of control winter wildfires in Colorado and lightning storms in Sydney Australia.
This could have been avoided if there were measurements in place to evacuate these people off the floodlines. Of course, people are building here because they have nowhere else to bolt. So we feel that government should evacuate these areas they have indicated that they will identify a area where it's safe to go for these people and evacuate.
But, says Ngwenya, the people have so far refused to move.
The people in duncan village are resisting to move for the reasons that we are very much aware of, they want to be close to the economic cities. And we don't want to say a situation of this nature is going to assist us in that process. But we are hoping that through the devastation that we've seen, it will be much easier to convince people that they need to move.
Mac: So the accusation that you might have acted slow a fair one?
Sam: I wouldn't look at any family member in the eye and defend that accusation. From our side, as government, we are trying to do our very best to try and assess the situation, we're not gonna bring anyone back.
On Wednesday Buffalo City was declared a disaster. That’ll give the city access to much needed funding from the national government as it attempts to rebuild.
The immediate relief will be mattresses, it will be blankets, it will be food, hygiene items, clothing, and gift to the givers you're standing in our warehouse.
As you can see our warehouse is empty as we've been distributing. But as soon as we done with this flooding in êast London will fill it up again and we'll prepare for the next disaster.

metadata.Further information: Then we come to the Eastern Cape which was hit hard this weekend: We can go there or we can send a camera man... its going to be hard to navigate with all the floods but a presenter could go and meet the camera man and get links, while i get the experts up here in joburg or i can go there too. Either way easy to do. On the ground we would go speak to rescuers, and victims of the floods... "The death toll from Saturday’s flash floods in the Eastern Cape has risen to seven. Mdantsane and Duncan Village were the hardest hit. Premier Oscar Mabuyane is working with ground teams to assess the full damage. His spokesperson Khuselwa Rantjie said the youngest drowning victim was just 19. Meanwhile, it's been confirmed that police rescue diver Captain Pierre Marx is the seventh death. Rantjie said the premier had conveyed his deepest respects to the late officer for his efforts." Strangely enough I have friends who know Capt Marx and can try get his family to do an interview. He seems a hell of a guy - and the story of how he first saved someone before drowning himself is heroic to say the least. I can contact my friend and the police contact Brigadier Tembinkosi Kinana 082 301 7699 about marx. He was part of the k9 search and rescue unit, and died in the line of duty. However, there are some excellent previous articles about him. his wife; https://www.facebook.com/michalene.b.marx One thought is that we can go with the daily dispatch out there and see them in action too. "Videos of heavy flooding in the Mdantsane area in the Buffalo City Municipality left South Africans stunned on Saturday night. Multiple bridges and roads were seen being completely engulfed by rapid water. Several houses and informal structures were also almost completely washed away. According to the East London Police, 53-year-old Captain Pierre Marx was attending to a complaint of drowning along with other rescue divers. Four people were swept off the Horse Shoe Valley causeway. Marx managed to rescue one, while his colleagues brought back three bodies “According to the report, the officers managed to take the three bodies across the stream. After a successful rescue of the complainant who is believed to be a local farmer, Captain Marx struggled with a strong current sweeping him despite attempts by his colleagues to rescue him. He disappeared in the heavy stream and only to be recovered in the early morning of Sunday the 09th January 2022.” EXPERTS ON LA NINA AT WEATHERSA: Dr Christien Engelbrecht; Lead Scientist: Long-range Forecasting: christien.engelbrecht@weathersa.co.za; cell 082 336 8293 Media enquiries: Ms Hannelee Doubell: Manager, Communications; Tel: (012) 367 6104; Cell: 072 222 6305; E-mail: hannelee.doubell@weathersa.co.za
